title: Fragmented trace reassembly protocol and minimal wire encoder
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Mobile / edge SDKs and unreliable networks frequently produce partial or fragmented trace data (chunked body uploads, intermittent connections, and background process suspensions). Current approach of dropping fragments or relying on full-span uploads creates high signal loss for low-latency edge services and inflight inference requests.

Proposal: Design and implement a compact, backwards-compatible fragmented-trace wire protocol plus a lightweight reassembly service that enables best-effort partial-span stitching and backfill. The protocol (FTW - Fragmented Trace Wire) will: 1) encode minimal fragment metadata (trace_id, span_id, fragment_seq, total_estimate_or_unknown, timestamp, ttl); 2) include a small content checksum and optional signature header for tamper detection; 3) allow fragments to be sent over unreliable transports (UDP-like or small HTTP/1 chunked retries) and reassembled server-side by a reassembly worker.

Goals: Reduce permanent telemetry loss on lossy networks by >=60% for mobile/edge clients while adding <80 bytes median overhead per request. Preserve sampling semantics and enable eventual backfill for missing sibling fragments when available. Maintain backward compat with older SDKs by falling back to current envelope behavior if FTW header absent.

Design notes / trade-offs: 
- Overhead vs fidelity: FTW adds a per-fragment header; we keep it minimal (fields listed above) and allow optional payload compression for larger spans.
- Security: Signatures are optional for low-end clients; enforce signature verification for Private deployments and Dedicated customers. KMS/HSM integration planned for signing key management.
- Reassembly semantics: Worker attempts deterministic merge and creates a "stitch score" (0.0-1.0) to mark completeness. Partial spans will be emitted with a metadata flag and shard-score so downstream dashboards/alerts can filter.
- Sampling: Respect original sample decision. If trace is unsampled, fragments are dropped locally. If sampled, fragments are sent with a sample_id. We must coordinate with sampling budget enforcer (ENG-403212) to avoid double-counting when fragments are reassembled/backfilled.
- Backwards compatibility: SDKs without FTW continue to send full envelopes. Server will accept both and normalize into the same internal span model.

Implementation plan: 
1) Wire spec doc (this ticket) -> RFC in Confluence: /display/OBS/FTW+Wire+Spec (link in comments).
2) Prototype reassembly worker (Go) that consumes fragments from a Kafka topic and writes reassembled spans to the telemetry ingestion pipeline. Deploy on staging.
3) Minimal JS and Python SDK adapters that add FTW headers and fragment small payloads when connection disruption observed.
4) Sidecar (optional) for on-prem Private installs that performs local reassembly to reduce cross-network noise.
5) Integrate stitch-score tag in Console traces UI and expose metrics for frag_reassembled_count, frag_dropped_count, avg_reassembly_latency.

Acceptance criteria: 
- FTW wire RFC merged and reviewed by Security and SDK leads.
- Prototype reassembly worker running in staging processing synthetic fragment streams.
- End-to-end test: sample mobile client can fragment a 3KB span into 4 fragments, reassemble in staging, and show a stitched trace in Console with correct trace_id and stitch-score >= 0.8.

Risks and mitigation: 
- Increased ingestion load: Use thresholded reassembly TTL and aggressive dedupe by fragment id/hash. Rate-limit reassembly for low-value customers.
- Privacy/PII: Ensure fragments follow the same scrubbing pipeline; avoid reassembling sensitive payloads without customer consent (configurable per tenant).

Next steps: 
- Post RFC to Confluence and request security review (due 2026-03-15).
- Open prototype repo and initial PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ftw-proto PR #42 (link in comments).
- Sync with SDK owners: schedule design review 2026-03-13.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the protocol and server-side reassembly. Separate follow-ups will cover Console UI changes for stitch-score visualization and Dedicated/Private sidecar packaging.
